extracted.intended_audience: Wellcome-funded researchers preparing submissions to Wellcome Open Research
extracted.subtask_description: Checklist and publisher requirements for preparing and submitting research articles (and non-traditional article types) to Wellcome Open Research, including eligibility, ethical and data policies, pre-publication checks, and reviewer suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: At least one author is funded or co-funded by the Wellcome Trust, or has been in the past, and the article is a result of this funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have your grant ID ready, as you will need to enter it on the submission form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / no duplicate publication
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles must be original and not duplications of work that has been published previously or is currently under consideration or review elsewhere for publication (excluding work posted on a pre-print server).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is significant overlap with another paper, this must be cited in the article and mentioned on submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: All listed authors must have made a clear contribution to an article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anyone who has contributed but does not meet the criteria for authorship can be listed in the 'Acknowledgements' section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarly nature of research
rubrics_metrics.description: All research must be scholarly work based on scientific, translational, applied, or clinical investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article-type specific requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome Open Research accepts a broad range of traditional and non-traditional article types (e.g., Research Articles, Data Notes, Software Tool Articles), and each article type has its own requirements to meet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should check the respective article guidelines for their work. Example: clinical trials within a Clinical Practice Article or Case Report need to be registered in an approved register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical approval and consent
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles must comply with the editorial ethical policies; appropriate ethics approval and consent must be obtained in advance where required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Work involving humans must adhere to the Declaration of Helsinki; research with animals must follow ARRIVE principles and comply with CITES; research involving plants must comply with the Convention on Biological Diversity and CITES.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-publication checks (editorial checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: The editorial team undertakes thorough pre-publication checks for each submitted article to ensure it meets requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks include competing interest statements, language quality, reproducibility/reporting standards, and data availability; editorial team may recommend changes (e.g., copyediting) before acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interest statement
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers must include a competing interest statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where competing interests are identified, this will not inhibit publication but will help provide full transparency for reviewers and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles need to be well-written, and language quality shouldn’t impede understanding of the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the editorial team thinks an article needs language editing to improve readability, they will recommend professional copyediting services before the paper can be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility and reporting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles must adhere to standards of reporting guidelines to provide a clear and comprehensive description of research, including clear methodological details to make it easier for others to assess and reproduce the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting standards can vary by article type (for example, specific guidelines exist for Systematic Reviews and clinical trials), so authors should review the relevant guidelines before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open data compliance (data policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome Open Research requires all data to comply with the journal’s open data policy, ensuring underlying data is made open where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open data enables reproducibility, transparency, visibility, and trust; one common reason for rejection is supporting data not being openly available. Authors are strongly encouraged to review the data policy before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAIR data principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable)
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal endorses the FAIR Data Principles to achieve open data: Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findable: host data in a stable open repository, assign a globally unique persistent identifier (e.g., DOI), and provide associated metadata. Accessible: publish under CC0 or an OSI-approved license for software/source code to enable reuse. Interoperable: store in non-proprietary open file formats and describe using standard vocabularies where available. Reusable: include metadata and additional documents so others can understand and reuse the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to open data
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that not all data can be made open (for example confidential, ethical or proprietary third‑party data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wellcome Open Research has specific policies to account for restricted data — authors should consult the data policy for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing and depositing data
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must prepare their data for sharing, deposit data in an appropriate repository, and add a Data Availability Statement to their article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These steps help meet open data guidelines; failure to make supporting data available is a common reason for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggesting suitable peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of submission authors need to suggest five suitable peer reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can select reviewers using the Wellcome Open Research reviewer finding algorithm (which scans the article and reference list to identify suitable reviewers) or choose their own reviewers. The editorial team will facilitate the peer review process, contact reviewers on the author’s behalf, and may suggest suitable reviewers where required. The site also provides tips for finding reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission via online form
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your research for publication using the journal’s online submission form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete required fields such as grant ID and suggested reviewers; submitting after following the checklist gives the work the best chance of being published in the current year.
